description:
If you have been following Gotham’s latest comic adventures, then you know that Scott Snyder's Absolute Batman has been an incredibly successful, brick-house take on the Caped Crusader. It’s no shocking surprise that TT Games' LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight would pay tribute to the massive new look by including a special unlockable Absolute Batman costume. While he might be a whole lot of Batman to fit into such a small minifigure, this guide will show you exactly how to complete the Chapter 2 "On the Prowl" side activities, track down the escaped zoo animals around Gotham City, and add this absolute unit of a suit to your inventory.

Looking for more LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight gameplay guides? This walkthrough breaks down the easiest methods to secure your new costume early in Chapter 2 or by utilizing Batgirl's radio towers in Chapter 4. title: Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight - How to Unlock the Absolute Batman Suit

author: IGN
description:
Early into your playthrough of LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, your mission to take down Carmine Falcone leads you straight into Gotham City's infamous Iceberg Lounge. While navigating the Penguin's territory, you'll stumble upon a locked vault hidden away in a back room. Cracking the code isn't just for show—inside lies a highly coveted Red Brick that unlocks a sleek cosmetic modifier for the Dark Knight's arsenal. If you're struggling to track down the clues or wrestle with the tricky safe dial controls, this quick puzzle guide has you covered. 

Our step-by-step walkthrough details exactly how to solve the Iceberg Lounge vault puzzle to claim your reward. We break down the locations of both hidden clues scattered across the bar and lounge area, reveal the final three-digit safe combination, and explain how to properly manipulate the analog stick inputs to unlock the door. title: Lego Batman Legacy of the Dark Knight: Iceberg Lounge Vault Puzzle Solution

author: IGN
description:
Batman was created more than 80 years ago and has starred in video games for 40 of them, nearly half of his existence, but the dozens of Batman games across countless platforms and console generations have rarely strayed far from the basics. No matter what decade it is, no matter what hardware you’re playing on, odds are that in any given Batman title you’ll be gliding off gargoyles, firing grappling hooks, and flinging Batarangs at guys in straightjackets. 

Batman’s constant reinventions in the comics have left the games mostly playing catch-up for the better part of their history, largely tied to popular movies and TV shows rather than taking the character someplace truly new, but within these constraints, and eventually beyond them, we’ve seen genuine masterpieces with the Batman Arkham series, slept-on gems, unmitigated disasters, and entries so bizarre and inexplicable they belong inside the Black Casebook. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight is the latest and most comprehens
title: The Complete History of Batman Games - Best, Worst, Weirdest

author: IGN
description: I've only played a couple hours of Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2, blasting through the 45-minute demo as both playable characters, but I've had a rousing time with it. Both characters feel different and exciting with punchy and satisfying weapons. The new level designs – particularly the icy one – have me intrigued to see what else they've cooked up. It's still very much what I'd expect when you say "Warhammer 40K" and "boomer shooter." But that remains a glorious combination. Previewed by Leana Hafer
title: Warhammer 40K: Boltgun 2 Hands-on Preview

author: IGN
description:
Hordes aren't a rare inconvenience in Canyons; they're the natural state of things. The Awakened pour in from everywhere: out of the sand, out of the ruins, down from the cliffs. And they almost never come alone — dozens at a time, sometimes hundreds.

There's never a shortage of reasons to fight either. A chance encounter on the road, a raid on your position, clearing a point of interest, holding off a fanatic siege — the canyon always has something new lined up. Enemy density scales with your squad size too, whether you're running solo or with a full crew of four Crusaders. 

Fighting that many enemies at once changes the logic of a gunfight entirely. One well-placed shot won't cut it anymore, and what matters now is position, tempo, and who's actually pulling their weight: who's holding the flank, who's covering the retreat, who threw that grenade, and who's just standing there looking useful. Every skirmish turns into a spectacle though, with bodies scattering, barrels going up, a
title: Canyons: Official Enemy Hordes Trailer

description: Welcome back to Next-Gen Console Watch! This week, Daemon and Max are joined by Nintendo Voice Chat's Logan Plant and Podcast Unlocked's Miranda Sanchez to give their predictions on the summer's big gaming showcases. Plus we have last episode's poll and a new poll for you to vote on at IGN.com and Spotify.

author: IGN
description:
Neon Genesis Evangelion is an iconic anime franchise that has stood that the test of time and fans can't seem to get enough EVA despite the creator Hideaki Anno's definitive ending to the final film. This is a retrospective taking a look back at the last 30 years of Evangelion, the fandom that grew up with it, can't grow up without it, and how creator Hideaki Anno has also grown as a fan and creator.

This retrospective take a look at the original Neon Genesis Evangelion animated series, The End of Evangelion, and the Rebuilds of Evangelion; including: Evangelion 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone, Evangelion 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance, 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo, and 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time, as well a look ahead at Yoko Taro's upcoming take on Evangelion with Nier Composer Keiichi Okabe.

#IGN #Anime
title: You Can (Not) Outgrow Neon Genesis Evangelion - A Retrospective
